opportunities.title: Google AI Essentials: Online Learning Circle
opportunities.description: Curious about artificial intelligence or want to learn practical AI skills for work and personal use? Join our staff-facilitated learning circle to complete the self-paced Google AI Essentials specialization. This 10-hour introductory-level specialization, offered through Coursera, is available for free to learning circle participants. It is made up of five courses, each containing four units that consist of short videos, articles, assignments and a short multiple-choice quiz. By completing the specialization, you will learn: How AI works How to write effective prompts How to use generative AI tools responsibly How to identify AI's potential biases and avoid harm How to stay up to date with AI news After you complete the course, you earn a Google certificate and a badge to share with others Learning Circles are study groups guided by library staff for people who want to complete the Google AI Essentials specialization together in a welcoming space: Learners meet weekly and work together through course materials. Participants are expected to commit to attending all four learning circle sessions. No AI experience is required. How to Joi n a Learning Circle: Register once on the first session of this event series, in order to attend all sessions. Please sign up with a valid email address . A valid TPL library card is required for online circles. Attend all four sessions online via Zoom, September 9, 16 and 23. Registration is a two-step procedure. First, participants must complete their registration through this page. After this step, library staff will follow up to request additional information in order to complete the registration. Information Collection Notice: The personal information on this form is collected by the Toronto Public Library under the Public Libraries Act, sections 20(a), 20(c), and 20(d). The information will only be used for event and program registration, delivery and evaluation. Questions about how the library handles your information can be directed to Answerline staff at answerline@tpl.ca , 416-397-5981, 789 Yonge Street, Toronto ON M4W 2G8.

opportunities.title: What the Heck is Roblox? Kids, KidTech and Digital Play
opportunities.description: Natalie Coulter, Associate Professor, Communication and Media Studies, Faculty of Liberal Arts and Professional Studies Drawing from her new book Kids, KidTech, and Digital Capitalism: The Fight for Our Digital Futures , Coulter explores what it means to be a child and how the experiences of childhood are shifting under the oppressive weight of digital capitalism. Using Roblox as a primary example, she illustrates how understanding children’s digital lives requires greater attention to the corporate infrastructures that shape their digital environments and how these influence what it means to grow up in a digital society.

opportunities.title: 3D Design a Nametag with Tinkercad
opportunities.description: Learn how to design a nametag with Tinkercad. This program will explore the fundamentals of 3D Design using a browser-based program, while completing a project. This is an in person event, no prior design experience is necessary. Attendants must pre-register a Tinkercad account in tinkercad.com, or have a google account, apple account or facebook account to log into the Tinkercad. Registration required. Intended for ages 13+. Each Child under 12 years old must accompany an adult. For safety reasons, no child under 6 years old will be allowed in this class. Information Collection Notice: The personal information on this form is collected by the Toronto Public Library under the Public Libraries Act, sections 20(a), 20(c), and 20(d). The information will only be used for event and program registration, delivery and evaluation. Questions about how the library handles your information can be directed to Answerline staff at answerline@tpl.ca , 416-397-5981, 789 Yonge Street, Toronto ON M4W 2G8.
opportunities.address: Fairview, 35 Fairview Mall Drive, Toronto, ON, M2J 4S4

opportunities.title: Computers for Beginners 1: Use the Mouse
opportunities.description: A class on how to use a mouse for absolute beginners with little or no computer experience. In this first session you will: Observe and practice how to operate a mouse effectively Understand various mouse pointers and cursors Review basic keyboard functions Use the mouse for basic Windows functions Upon completion of this class students will be able to use a computer mouse at a basic level and will be able to go online for additional practice. Prerequisites: No computer experience required. Format: Hands-on with demonstrations

opportunities.description: Turn a plain mug into a masterpiece! Join us for a hands-on workshop where you will learn to use Cricut machine to design, cut, and press your very own custom mug. Space is limited. Please arrive at 3:30pm to secure your spot in the program. Participants must be available both dates to ensure completion of project. This program is part of Youth Hub service. Youth Hubs are a welcoming place for teens after school and in the summer, where helpful staff are always available. Free, nutritious snacks are offered daily. Drop by a branch with a Youth Hub or call the branch to find out more. Information Collection Notice: The personal information on this form is collected by the Toronto Public Library under the Public Libraries Act, sections 20(a), 20(c), and 20(d). The information will only be used for event and program registration, delivery and evaluation. Questions about how the library handles your information can be directed to Answerline staff at answerline@tpl.ca , 416-397-5981, 789 Yonge Street, Toronto ON M4W 2G8.

opportunities.title: Summer STEM
opportunities.description: Join us for some fun STEM-based projects in our summer STEM series. Each session will feature an exciting STEM activity for kids to complete. Registration is required. For ages 8-12 only (children outside of this age range will not be able to participate). *For all registered Children's programs at Malvern, there is a grace period of 10 minutes. After the first 10 minutes of a program, spots will be given to waiting customers.* Information Collection Notice: The personal information on this form is collected by the Toronto Public Library under the Public Libraries Act, sections 20(a), 20(c), and 20(d). The information will only be used for event and program registration, delivery and evaluation. Questions about how the library handles your information can be directed to Answerline staff at answerline@tpl.ca , 416-397-5981, 789 Yonge Street, Toronto ON M4W 2G8.

opportunities.title: Intro to 3D Printing & Design with Tinkercad
opportunities.description: A hands-on workshop where participants will learn how 3D Printing works and use Tinkercad to explore 3D design basics. New to 3D Printing and Design? Come and watch and learn from TPL Staff on how a 3D printer works in the Digital Innovation Hub. Class instruction includes: How to prepare a 3D design file for print How to use the equipment properly and safely Reviewing the rules and guidelines to using the 3D printer Followed by the introduction to printing, class participants will be given a hands-on workshop where they learn how to create simple 3D designed key chain and become familiar with design tools. Registration is required for this class. You can order free tickets by clicking the link below. Tickets will become available one week prior to the class at 9 a.m. It is strongly recommended that you create at Tinkercad.com ahead of the session. Information Collection Notice: The personal information on this form is collected by the Toronto Public Library under the Public Libraries Act, sections 20(a), 20(c), and 20(d). The information will only be used for event and program registration, delivery and evaluation. Questions about how the library handles your information can be directed to Answerline staff at answerline@tpl.ca , 416-397-5981, 789 Yonge Street, Toronto ON M4W 2G8.

opportunities.title: Introduction to Ancient and Modern Cosmology with Dr. Ting Li
opportunities.description: Celebrate Astronomy Day with Fort York! Dr. Ting Li (Dunlap Institute, University of Toronto) will be joining us to give a talk on Ancient and Modern Cosmology. Through this talk you will gain an understanding of cosmology, both ancient and modern. We will explore the history of how humans have sought to explain the origins and structure of the universe, from ancient myths to modern scientific theories. Join us to learn about the latest discoveries and theories in cosmology, including dark matter, dark energy, and the big bang. Drop-in. First come, first served.

opportunities.title: Resilience Reads: a climate neighbourhood reading party
opportunities.description: Join us to share the joy of reading, while building climate resilience knowledge. Members are invited to discuss a book they are reading, tell stories, and empower each other to explore community-driven solutions. Each party will start with a quiet read and reflect time, with opportunities to join group discussions later on over refreshments. APRIL 15-Learning from trees for Earth Month The Overstory by Richard Power MAY 20-All women are water defenders Memory of Water by Emmi Itaranta or your favourite book featuring water! JUNE 17– Righting our relationship with land Earth Keeper by N. Scott Momaday or your favourite book that shares how words are medicine! JULY 15– Climate migration or the borders between us are not lines that divide us, but seams that connect us Gun Island / The Hungry Tide by Amitav Ghosh or your favourite island setting summer read! Copies are available in the branch to pick up, while supplies last. AUGUST 19--Fossil Fuel Folly American War by Omar El Akkad or your favourite dystopian read! SEPTEMBER 16--We Need Pollinators The History of Bees by Maja Lunde or your favourite animal-centred book! OCTOBER 21--Climate Change is Scary The Annual Migration of Clouds by Premee Mohamed or a different book that shares a scary future ecological crisis! NOVEMBER 18--Climate changes everything The Ministry for the Future by Kim Stanley Robinson or your favourite time travel read! Information Collection Notice: The personal information on this form is collected by the Toronto Public Library under the Public Libraries Act, sections 20(a), 20(c), and 20(d). The information will only be used for event and program registration, delivery and evaluation. Questions about how the library handles your information can be directed to Answerline staff at answerline@tpl.ca , 416-397-5981, 789 Yonge Street, Toronto ON M4W 2G8.

No registration required. Information Collection Notice: The personal information on this form is collected by the Toronto Public Library under the Public Libraries Act, sections 20(a), 20(c), and 20(d). opportunities.title: Python Essentials 2 Learning Circle
opportunities.description: Take an intermediate Python course to advance your programming skills. This learning circle will meet online on Thursday afternoons, 2-3:30pm for August 6 to September 24. Learning circles are study groups guided by staff for people who want to take a free online course together in a welcoming space. Learners meet weekly to complete the course together. Participants are expected to commit to the duration of the course and attend all learning circle sessions. Python Essentials 2 is designed for learners who are already familiar with the essentials of Python, including programming concepts like data types, containers, functions, conditions, and loops. Required: completion of the Python Essentials 1 course, or equivalent experience. Python Essentials 2 is the second in a 2-course series that will prepare you for the PCAP – Certified Associate in Python Programming certification exam at Pearson VUE. This intermediate-level course covers advanced aspects of Python programming , including modules, packages, exceptions, file processing, as well as general coding techniques and object-oriented programming (OOP). For more information about the Python Essentials 2 learning circle, please contact networkingacademy@tpl.ca Information Collection Notice: The personal information on this form is collected by the Toronto Public Library under the Public Libraries Act, sections 20(a), 20(c), and 20(d). The information will only be used for event and program registration, delivery and evaluation. Questions about how the library handles your information can be directed to Answerline staff at answerline@tpl.ca , 416-397-5981, 789 Yonge Street, Toronto ON M4W 2G8.

They will start with simple components such as LEDs, motors, and resistors, and gradually progress to more complex circuits involving sensors, wireless control, and LCD displays. This program is only for children aged 9 to 12 years. Registration is required. Please only register the children that will be participating, accompanying adults do not need to register. Information Collection Notice: The personal information on this form is collected by the Toronto Public Library under the Public Libraries Act, sections 20(a), 20(c), and 20(d). opportunities.title: After School Club
opportunities.description: Looking for something to do after school? Come out to our After School Club and learn new things, make stuff, meet other kids and have fun! For children ages 6-12 years old. Please note: some programs begin 15 minutes early to allow for two separate sessions for younger and older children. Between 3:30 and 4:00, snacks are offered during the After School Club for participants. Ingredient lists will be available. Snacks are generously supported, in part, by donors. T hursday, September 17: Robotic Fun, 2 SESSIONS: Juniors (ages 6 & 7) 3:45 - 4:25 pm Seniors (ages 8 +) 4:30 - 5:15 pm Thursday, September 24: Snap Circuits, 2 SESSIONS Juniors (ages 6 & 7) 3:45 - 4:25 pm Seniors (ages 8+) 4:30 - 5:15 pm Thursday, October 1: Board Games Thursday, October 8: Building Challenges Thursday, October 15: Pawsitivley Pets Learn about animals in a fun and interactive way. Live animals will be part of the presentation. For children ages 4 and up.

opportunities.description: Learn how to customize your 3D designs by using SVG files in this class! Participants will learn about transparent backgrounds and converting png images into SVGs. Using TinkerCAD, they will turn the 2D image into a 3D personalized keychain ready for printing. Registration is required via tpl.ca. Information Collection Notice: The personal information on this form is collected by the Toronto Public Library under the Public Libraries Act, sections 20(a), 20(c), and 20(d). The information will only be used for event and program registration, delivery and evaluation. Questions about how the library handles your information can be directed to Answerline staff at answerline@tpl.ca , 416-397-5981, 789 Yonge Street, Toronto ON M4W 2G8.

opportunities.title: Google AI Essentials: In Person Learning Circle
opportunities.description: Curious about artificial intelligence or want to learn practical AI skills for work and personal use? Join our staff-facilitated learning circle to complete the self-paced Google AI Essentials specialization. This 10-hour introductory-level specialization, offered through Coursera, is available for free to learning circle participants. It is made up of five courses, each containing four units that consist of short videos, articles, assignments and a short multiple-choice quiz. By completing the specialization, you will learn: How AI works How to write effective prompts How to use generative AI tools responsibly How to identify AI's potential biases and avoid harm How to stay up to date with AI news After you complete the course, you earn a Google certificate and a badge to share with others Learning Circles are study groups guided by library staff for people who want to complete the Google AI Essentials specialization together in a welcoming space: Learners meet weekly and work together through course materials. Participants are expected to commit to attending all four learning circle sessions. No AI experience is required. How to Join a Learning Circle: Register once on the first session of this event series, in order to attend all sessions. Please sign up with a valid email address . A valid TPL library card is required for online circles. Attend all four sessions in person at Northern District Branch . Registration is a two-step procedure. First, participants must complete their registration through this page. After this step, library staff will follow up to request additional information in order to complete the registration. Information Collection Notice: The personal information on this form is collected by the Toronto Public Library under the Public Libraries Act, sections 20(a), 20(c), and 20(d). The information will only be used for event and program registration, delivery and evaluation. Questions about how the library handles your information can be directed to Answerline staff at answerline@tpl.ca , 416-397-5981, 789 Yonge Street, Toronto ON M4W 2G8.
opportunities.address: Northern District, 40 Orchard View Boulevard, Toronto, ON, M4R 1B9

opportunities.description: Are you interested in improving your computer skills? Join our beginner and intermediate Microsoft Word and PowerPoint classes. opportunities.title: Cyanotype Workshop
opportunities.description: What materials and processes existed before Adobe Photoshop? Join us for a hands-on analog image making workshop to create a Cyanotype. The Cyanotype is a photographic printing technique sensitive to a limited near ultraviolet and blue light spectrum. It involves layering objects and transparencies. All are welcome! We will supply all materials, but feel free to bring an object or 2D silhouette for a contact print. opportunities.title: Google Prompting Essentials: Online Learning Circle
opportunities.description: Ready to develop the skills to use generative AI (GenAI) tools effectively and responsibly for work and daily life? Join our staff-facilitated Learning Circle to complete the self-paced Google Prompting specialization. By completing this Learning Circle program, you will earn a Google Prompting Essentials certificate to share on your resume, LinkedIn and social media profiles! What You'll Learn This program is designed for those with some experience with using GenAI. Through short videos, articles, assignments and quizzes, you will discover: Essential Prompting Skills : How to use a prompting framework to create a desired output with GenAI; how to evaluate and refine your results. Everyday Work Tasks: Strategies to draft content, brainstorm ideas, create tables, timelines, and more. Data & Presentations: How to explore data visualization and use GenAI responsibly when working with data. Advanced Techniques: How to use prompt chaining for complex tasks and prompt versioning to save and reuse your best prompts over time. Learning Circles are study groups guided by library staff for people who want to complete the Google Prompting specialization together in a welcoming space: Learners meet weekly and work together through course materials. Participants are expected to commit to attending all four Learning Circle sessions. Some Experience with GenAI Recommended: This course is ideal for participants who have completed the AI Essentials course Learning Circle. How to Joi n a Learning Circle: Register once for the first session of this event series, in order to attend all sessions. Please sign up with a valid email address. A valid TPL library card is required for online circles. Attend all four sessions online via Zoom, Friday September 11, 18, 25 and Oct 2, from 1:30-4PM. Registration is a two-step process. First, participants must complete their registration through this page. After this step, library staff will follow up to request additional information in order to complete the registration. Information Collection Notice: The personal information on this form is collected by the Toronto Public Library under the Public Libraries Act, sections 20(a), 20(c), and 20(d). The information will only be used for event and program registration, delivery and evaluation. Questions about how the library handles your information can be directed to Answerline staff at answerline@tpl.ca , 416-397-5981, 789 Yonge Street, Toronto ON M4W 2G8.

opportunities.title: Homeschoolers Weekly Meet-Up @ Angus Glen
opportunities.description: Are you a homeschooler family? Markham Public Library hosts weekly meetups for homeschooler families on Monday mornings at the Angus Glen Library Branch from 10:30AM - 12:00PM . These meetups give participating caregivers and children an opportunity to connect with other homeschooling families, work together to explore various STEAM building and literacy development focused activities, learn about library resources, meet special guest speakers, and more! Introduction to the Makerspace (with a Glowforge Laser Engraver Demo & Group Activity) *** Pls note that this session is generally geared towards older children and adults. Extra colouring sheets & activities are available for younger children. *** PLEASE NOTE: Adults (caregivers) are responsible for supervising and assisting the children in their care with all planned activities and/or exercises Most planned activities are suitable for ages 5+ and may be subject to change Active participation and engagement of all caregivers is required ⚠️ PLEASE REGISTER TO ATTEND: We require advance registration for this program due to limited space, room capacity, and to support the library in our ability to plan activities and prepare supplies. We ask that all participants (caregivers and children) please sign-up for each session to guarantee your spot! *** ***For example, if there is 1 caregiver and 3 children attending, please indicate 4 in the registration.
opportunities.address: Angus Glen Branch, 3990 Major Mackenzie Drive East, Markham, Ontario, L6C 1P8

opportunities.description: Curious about the Cricut? In this introductory class, participants will explore the creative possibilities of this popular cutting machine. You’ll also see a demonstration of the machine in action, showing how easy it is to design and cut custom creations. Perfect for anyone looking to get started with the Cricut and learn more about how you can use the Cricut in our makerspace!

opportunities.description: Join Family Services York Region for a practical Back-to-School Reset! This session is facilitated in Mandarin and is perfect for newcomer families. Gain tools for smoother transitions and balanced tech use. Participants will learn: How to establish healthy family routines. How to manage screen time. How to build positive digital habits that support your child’s success in schools. 開學了，如何幫助孩子收心？ 總是為了手機、電腦和孩子吵架？ 誠邀您參加 「 開學收心指南」實用講座！ 一起解鎖健康家庭作息、合理控管螢幕時間，培養健康的電子產品使用習慣。 *The program's facilitator also speaks Cantonese*

opportunities.title: Homeschoolers Weekly Meet-Up @ Angus Glen
opportunities.description: Are you a homeschooler family? Markham Public Library hosts weekly meetups for homeschooler families on Monday mornings at the Angus Glen Library Branch from 10:30AM - 12:00PM . These meetups give participating caregivers and children an opportunity to connect with other homeschooling families, work together to explore various STEAM building and literacy development focused activities, learn about library resources, meet special guest speakers, and more! Passive Worksheets (Wordsearches & Colouring) + Kapla Blocks & Challenge Cards + Guest Speaker Day speaker from City of Markham's Environmental Services, 11am-12 noon PLEASE NOTE: Adults (caregivers) are responsible for supervising and assisting the children in their care with all planned activities and/or exercises Most planned activities are suitable for ages 5+ and may be subject to change Active participation and engagement of all caregivers is required ⚠️ PLEASE REGISTER TO ATTEND: We require advance registration for this program due to limited space, room capacity, and to support the library in our ability to plan activities and prepare supplies. We ask that all participants (caregivers and children) please sign-up for each session to guarantee your spot! *** ***For example, if there is 1 caregiver and 3 children attending, please indicate 4 in the registration.
opportunities.address: Angus Glen Branch, 3990 Major Mackenzie Drive East, Markham, Ontario, L6C 1P8

opportunities.title: Makerspace Tour: Markham Village
opportunities.description: Join us in celebrating Digital Innovation Month by attending our Makerspace Tour Series! Are you curious about the makerspace ? Not sure what you can expect out of them? Whether you want to scan your great-grandparent's slides, make your own coasters with the laser engraver, 3D Print a t-rex or record your first album, there are many ways Markham Public Library can help you inspire you and get you started on your path to being a maker. Now is your chance to visit any of our five unique Makerspaces to meet our dedicated Digital Literacy Specialists, and learn about the tools and services available to you! Note: This is in a drop-in tour - arrive when you can, and stay as long as you want!

opportunities.title: Introduction to Recording Voiceover for Film in Audacity
opportunities.description: Want to learn how to add custom audio to your films and videos? Perhaps a voiceover? Join us in our Introduction to Recording Voiceover for Film in Audacity workshop! Audacity is an easy-to-use, multi-track audio editor and recorder for Windows, macOS, GNU/Linux and other operating systems. Audacity is a Digital Audio Workstation (DAW) that is FREE to download. This makerspace demonstration will provide instruction on how to use this program to get you started with sound editing and recording. We will cover how to edit sound, what effects this program has to offer on your vocals and how to mix down your different tracks. opportunities.description: Learn how to preserve your memories by converting 35mm slides or negatives into high resolution digital images. This demonstration introduces the process of scanning 35mm slides, and AI-powered restoration/modification techniques to remove deterioration and correcting the images' colours. Participants will leave with the knowledge needed to begin digitizing and restoring their own slide collections. Learning outcomes: Learn how to scan and digitize 35mm slides (or negatives) using Makerspace equipment Use AI tools to enhance scanned images by correcting colour and removing common imperfections Note: Program may allow drop-in participants, if space allows. Become Maker Certified Please note: if you are looking to use our makerspaces independently, you must be 13+ and complete this online Makerspace module . Once completed, our staff can update your profile and you will be maker certified! Check out the other Digital Innovation Month Tours and Programs - all happening this month: Markham Village: Tour Demo - Introduction to Recording Voiceover for Film in Audacity Thornhill Community Centre Tour Demo - Digitizing & Restoring 35mm Slides with AI Aaniin Tour Workshop - Cricut - Make an MPL Canvas Tote Bag Angus Glen Tour Workshop - How to Laser Engrave a Wooden Magnet with The Glowforge (4/5 - Digital Innovation Month Makerspace Series) Cornell Tour Demo #1 - Creating a Customized Puzzle with a Sublimation Printer - 11am Demo #2 - Creating a Customized Puzzle with a Sublimation Printer - 3pm

opportunities.title: Makerspace Tour: Thornhill Community Centre
opportunities.description: Join us in celebrating Digital Innovation Month by attending our Makerspace Tour Series! Are you curious about the makerspace ? Not sure what you can expect out of them? Whether you want to scan your great-grandparent's slides, make your own coasters with the laser engraver, 3D Print a t-rex or record your first album, there are many ways Markham Public Library can help you inspire you and get you started on your path to being a maker. Now is your chance to visit any of our five unique Makerspaces to meet our dedicated Digital Literacy Specialists, and learn about the tools and services available to you! Note: This is in a drop-in tour - arrive when you can, and stay as long as you want!

opportunities.title: Be An Active Digital Citizen - Play-based Workshop for Families
opportunities.description: In this play-based, interactive workshop for children and families, we explore what it means to be a smart, safe, and empowered digital citizen. Through games and hands-on activities, children will practice healthy social media habits and learn about their digital rights online in a fun, age-appropriate way. At the end of this workshop, participants should: Be able to recognize healthy vs. unhealthy social media habits and practice simple strategies for balanced use. Understand basic digital rights for children online (i.e. privacy, safety, expression). Build confidence identifying safe, respectful ways to engage with others online, both individually and as a family. Note: this session is intended to be intended by families including children aged 8 - 16 and their parents/caregivers . Please register for each individual attending. Hosted by Kids Rights Canada .

opportunities.title: Discover a Career in Science/Health Care
opportunities.description: Are you interested in starting a career in the field of health care? Or perhaps you work in the health care field and are looking to add to your education to move into a new area of health care? We’ll highlight important things such as: We will cover programs such as Personal Support Worker, Practical Nursing, Registered Nursing and Medical Device Reprocessing We will cover programs in the field of Science We will touch on entrance requirements, steps to apply A bit about financial aid and student supports **Please note: This workshop is run in partnership with Seneca Polytechnic**. _______ Registrants will receive an email with the Zoom link 1 day prior to the program. If you do not receive the Zoom link the day before the program: Check your email inbox and spam folders. If you still cannot find the email, please contact us at mplcommunitylibrarians@markhamlibrary.ca prior to the program start time so we can provide you with the link.

opportunities.title: CyberSafe Seniors, Preventing AI Fraud and Scams
opportunities.description: CyberSafe Seniors, Preventing AI Fraud and Scams which addresses the growing threat of AI-enabled online fraud and scams targeting older Canadians. As AI tools become more accessible, scammers are using tactics such as voice cloning, deepfake videos, and highly convincing phishing techniques to impersonate loved ones and fabricate financial emergencies. Older adults aged 55+ are disproportionately targeted, often experiencing significant financial loss along with shame, anxiety, and social isolation. Through workshops delivered by MediaSmarts experts participants will learn how AI-enabled scams work, how to verify messages from family or financial institutions, and what steps to take if targeted.

opportunities.title: STEM in Action - Engineering Activities: Aerospace
opportunities.description: Aerospace Engineering: Landing Rockets! In this workshop, students will explore the challenges of spacecraft landings by designing and testing a protective landing system for a model rocket carrying a delicate payload. Using the Engineering Design Process, participants will investigate forces, stability, and energy absorption while building, testing, and improving their designs through multiple landings. Discover how aerospace engineers design systems that enable safe landings on other planets Learning Outcomes Understand the role of landing systems for spacecrafts Identify and apply basic engineering design principles such as momentum, energy, drag, and absorption in a building challenge. Build, test, and improve the design of a rocket prototype Participants: Children aged 8 - 13 years old Note: Please sign up for each of the four sessions for your child(ren) to be able to attend all four unique sessions in this program series.

opportunities.title: How We Stay Relevant in the Age of AI
opportunities.description: AI is changing how people think about work, learning, and human value. Many professionals, parents, students, and community members are asking a very real question: if AI can generate answers, summaries, explanations, drafts, code, and ideas so quickly, where do humans remain relevant? This session argues that humans should not try to compete with AI at speed, recall, or routine output. That is the wrong competition. As AI makes answers easier to produce, human value moves toward deeper understanding, disciplined curiosity, judgment, and the ability to question, verify, and ground what AI produces. For most of us, learning has often been treated as natural and implicit. We were taught subjects in school, but not always taught how learning itself works. Machine learning gives us a useful mirror. In order to teach machines how to learn, humans had to make parts of learning explicit: objectives, data, patterns, prediction, feedback, error correction, validation, calibration, and updating. This session uses those machine learning principles not as a technical lesson, but as a way to think about how humans can learn more deeply in the age of AI. Participants will explore why superficial knowledge is becoming less survivable, why AI still needs to be grounded in human reality, and how disciplined curiosity can help people remain valuable as AI becomes more capable. The session will include a short lecture-style presentation followed by a guided audience discussion. The discussion can be shaped around a small number of reflection questions, with flexibility to shift into Q&A or a brief example/demo depending on the audience engagement and MPL’s preference. No technical background is required. By the end of this session, participants will be able to: Explain why shallow learning and routine knowledge work become more vulnerable when AI can generate fluent answers quickly. Apply key machine learning principles, such as objective-setting, feedback, error correction, validation, calibration, and updating, as a practical framework for deeper human learning, better questioning, and stronger judgment. Bio: Darren Soo is a Canadian technology founder and creator of PI, an individualized AI reasoning framework designed to help people reason through complex, changing information over time. His background spans more than two decades of practical technology work across enterprise and operational software environments. His current work centres on artificial intelligence, machine learning, and explainable reasoning systems, while his broader interests include how technology can support curiosity, better questions, learning and decision-making.
